items.title: Trump diz que EUA podem permanecer no Irã e ficar com petróleo
items.author: Bo Erickson, Conor Humphries
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Conor Humphries
items.summary: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, sugeriu neste domingo que os EUA podem permanecer no Irã e “ficar com o petróleo”, traçando um paralelo com a tentativa do país de assumir o controle de um quinto das vastas reservas de petróleo da Venezuela.
items.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, sugeriu neste domingo que os EUA podem permanecer no Irã e “ficar com o petróleo”, traçando um paralelo com a tentativa do país de assumir o controle de um quinto das vastas reservas de petróleo da Venezuela.
Durante uma viagem à Irlanda para reuniões e para assistir a partidas de golfe, ele reiterou que ainda espera que a guerra no Irã termine este ano, possivelmente logo após as eleições legislativas de meio de mandato previstas para novembro nos Estados Unidos.
Falando no campeonato de golfe Irish Open, Trump acrescentou que o preço da gasolina “cairia vertiginosamente” assim que a guerra no Irã terminasse.
A turbulência no Oriente Médio tem abalado os mercados de petróleo, com os operadores do setor esperando que os preços voltem a subir na segunda-feira, após um ataque a um oleoduto saudita.
Trump afirmou que só fecharia o “acordo certo” e não aceitará um que seja “ruim”, acrescentando que o Irã está “pedindo constantemente” por negociações de paz — uma afirmação que Teerã já rejeitou no passado.
Mas o presidente também apresentou outra opção: manter o diálogo com o Irã. Ele traçou um paralelo com o acordo dos EUA com a Venezuela, anunciado em agosto.
“No fim das contas, vamos sair (do Irã), a menos que decidamos ficar e ficar com o petróleo, como na Venezuela”, disse Trump, acrescentando que a receita obtida pelos EUA na Venezuela “pagou a guerra muitas vezes”.
(Reportagem de Bo Erickson, em Doonbeg, e Padraic Halpin e Conor Humphries, em Dublin)

items.title: Israel y el Líbano se reunirán en Roma en octubre, dice funcionario del Departamento de Estado EEUU
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Israel y el Líbano se reunirán en Roma en octubre para debatir un acuerdo de seguridad negociado por Estados Unidos con el objetivo de aliviar las hostilidades a lo largo de la frontera, dijo a Reuters un responsable del Departamento de Estado.
items.body:
Israel y el Líbano se reunirán en Roma en octubre para debatir un acuerdo de seguridad negociado por Estados Unidos con el objetivo de aliviar las hostilidades a lo largo de la frontera, dijo a Reuters un responsable del Departamento de Estado.
La aplicación continuada del acuerdo "sigue siendo el único mecanismo viable para restablecer la soberanía del Líbano y la seguridad de Israel", dijo el funcionario, que añadió que los embajadores libanés e israelí se reunirán en Washington la próxima semana.
La séptima ronda de negociaciones en la capital italiana concluyó en agosto sin que se lograra ningún avance en cuestiones territoriales clave.
Hezbolá e Israel volvieron a entrar en guerra el 2 de marzo en medio de un conflicto regional más amplio.
El Ejército israelí ocupa lo que describe como una "zona de contención" de unos 10 km (6 millas) de profundidad en el Líbano a lo largo de toda la frontera israelí. Las autoridades israelíes dicen que la zona es necesaria para proteger a las comunidades del norte de Israel de los ataques lanzados por Hezbolá.
Más de 4.300 personas han perdido la vida a causa de los ataques israelíes en el Líbano desde marzo, según el Ministerio de Salud libanés.

items.title: Lille go top as Lens rally to draw 2-2 at Le Mans
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Last season’s runners-up RC Lens fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 at promoted Le Mans on Sunday, while Lille went top of the Ligue 1 standings after an easy 2-0 triumph over Troyes.
items.body:
Last season’s runners-up RC Lens fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 at promoted Le Mans on Sunday, while Lille went top of the Ligue 1 standings after an easy 2-0 triumph over Troyes.
The victory put Lille top with 10 points from four matches, ahead of Monaco and Rennes on goal difference.
Lens, who had lost two of their opening three fixtures of the campaign, moved to four points while Le Mans are still looking for their first win of the season.
Le Mans looked in command in the first half at Stade Marie-Marvingt after Adil Bourabaa headed home a rebound after Louis Mafouta’s effort bounced back off the crossbar in the 32nd minute and then a quick counter-attack allowed Lucas Calodat to double their advantage in the 44th minute.
Lens pulled one back from tall Senegalese striker Abdallah Sima in stoppage time before the break and then equalised with another header, this time from substitute Franjo Ivanovic six minutes into the second half.
Thorgan Hazard hammered a free kick against the crossbar in the 80th minute as Lens came within inches of completing a turnaround.
Lille bounced back after their home loss to Real Betis in the Champions League in midweek to easily beat Troyes in a one-sided encounter at Stade Pierre-Mauroy.
Fullback Tiago Santos scored for a second time this season as he curled a first-time, right-footed shot into the far top corner.
Ethan Mbappe, sent off in the Champions League in midweek, came on as a substitute to add the second goal in stoppage time.
Later on Sunday, champions Paris St Germain will seek their first league win of the season as they visit Stade Brestois.

items.title: Bolt unfazed by robot's record run, eyes Manchester derby instead
items.author: Lori Ewing
items.creator: Lori Ewing
items.summary: Most athletes might bristle at seeing their records being broken. When eight-time Olympic champion Usain Bolt learned that a robot in China had eclipsed his 100-metres world record by almost a second, he was rather amused by the turn of events.
items.body:
Most athletes might bristle at seeing their records being broken. When eight-time Olympic champion Usain Bolt learned that a robot in China had eclipsed his 100-metres world record by almost a second, he was rather amused by the turn of events.
"It's just one of those things. I guess that's where the world is going right now," the Jamaican said with a laugh and a shrug. "It just made me smile."
A couple of weeks ago, "Robot beats Bolt" was splashed across headlines after [USN:L8N44N18V TEXT:"Tiangong Ultra"] won the 100m final at the second World Humanoid Robot Games, clocking 8.64 seconds, almost a second faster than Bolt's 9.58 world-record set in 2009.
The 40-year-old Bolt was in relaxed form as he met reporters in Budapest on the final day of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship, delivering a stream of anecdotes and one-liners that showed why he remains one of athletics' most magnetic personalities.
Although from the outset, Bolt appeared keen to wrap things up early.
"United is playing right now (versus City in the Manchester derby)," said the lifelong Manchester United supporter. "Very important time."
Bolt also reflected on his place in sporting history and how he hoped to be remembered, saying his ambition was never simply to dominate athletics, but to transcend it.
"My goal was always to be among the greats in sports," he said. "That when the conversation is being talked about Muhammad Ali ... and all these greats in different sports, I'm mentioned in that sentence. I'm happy that I'm actually in the conversation."
Bolt scolded reporters who had suggested at last year's world championships in Tokyo that he was out of shape.
"First of all, I made a joke and you guys took it out of context. It was everywhere!" he said. "I wasn't running out of breath walking up the stairs. I was just making a joke. I'm in the best shape of my life, guys."
His declaration drew laughter around the room.
"Listen, 'he's in the best shape of his life'. That's the headline," he said laughing before adding that he still works out daily.
Bolt flirted with a football career, but it ended in 2018 after a two-month trial with Australian club Central Coast Mariners, where he scored twice in a friendly on his first start.
But he had no answer for how his name was recently linked to Wythenshawe Vets FC, a Sunday league team in south Manchester that has gained attention for recruiting former Premier League players.
While Wythenshawe's supposed superstar signing made headlines, Bolt insisted he first learned about it when his longtime agent Ricky Simms contacted him.
"Ricky texted me and said, 'Are you playing football now?' And I was like, 'I don't know what's going on'."
Simms offered his own explanation.
"I think they wanted to have the option if he's ever in Manchester and wants to play."
And if any non-league club is still holding out hope of signing the fastest man in history, Bolt sounded in no rush to dust off his boots, preferring instead to keep an eye on Manchester United and enjoy retirement.

items.title: Haaland strike gives 10-man Man City contentious 1-0 derby win over Man United
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Erling Haaland scored in the second half to give 10-man Manchester City a 1-0 Premier League win at bitter rivals Manchester United on Sunday, with the strike initially disallowed for offside before the decision was overturned following a lengthy and contentious VAR review.
items.body:
Erling Haaland scored in the second half to give 10-man Manchester City a 1-0 Premier League win at bitter rivals Manchester United on Sunday, with the strike initially disallowed for offside before the decision was overturned following a lengthy and contentious VAR review.
The match had burst into life with the sending-off of City's Phil Foden in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, yet it was United who ended the encounter feeling hard done by.
Haaland was flagged offside after steering Josko Gvardiol’s cross into the net from a tight angle in the 60th minute, but replays showed that Patrick Dorgu’s outstretched foot had played the Norwegian onside.
The review was prolonged by the involvement of Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position and launched himself at the cross without making contact. The VAR ruled the goal could stand, however, even though Fernandez's attempt appeared to affect Lisandro Martinez’s efforts to cut out the delivery.
The game simmered for the opening period before the sending-off of Foden for kicking Fernandes in the stomach from a prone position. Though the kick lacked power, it made no difference to referee Michael Oliver, who brandished the red card.
Enzo Maresca's side retreated into a compact defensive block, and initially appeared comfortable despite their numerical disadvantage, although they offered little threat going forward.
Marcus Rashford almost gave the home side the lead just before the break when Fernandez conceded a free kick outside the box, but the winger's effort struck the left-hand post.
NO OFFSIDE OFFENCE United hit the woodwork again six minutes after the restart when Kobbie Mainoo let fly from distance, but the momentum shifted on the hour as Haaland steered Gvardiol’s cross home from a tight angle.
The assistant referee’s flag cut short City’s celebrations, only for VAR to rule that Dorgu had played Haaland onside and that Fernandez’s unsuccessful attempt to reach the ball did not constitute an offside offence.
City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma made a tremendous save in stoppage time to deny Bryan Mbeumo as City held on for a win that leaves them second in the table on 12 points from four games, behind champions Arsenal on goal difference, while United are 13th with four points from four games.
"It's a kind of new experience to win with 10 men and it's amazing, I have to be honest," Haaland told broadcaster Sky Sports.
"We need fighters in the team, which we have plenty of ... I'm super happy with every single one, and I'm so so proud of everyone ... I think we even became sharper when we became 10 men. That's how we have to play all the time, with 11 men as well."
Haaland admitted he had initially been unsure why the goal was allowed to stand.
"I think there was a flick, so I thought maybe there was someone who flicked it, because I normally don't go offside. So I told Michael Oliver I took it a bit personally that he thought it was offside," he joked.
"But I looked over to Enzo, the gaffer, and he gave me a thumbs up and then I kind of knew that it was a goal, so I prepared myself a bit to celebrate."

items.title: Trump diz a Zelenskiy para parar de atacar diesel russo
items.author: Bo Erickson
items.creator: Bo Erickson
items.summary: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, disse neste domingo ao presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, que pare de atacar a infraestrutura russa de diesel, afirmando que os ataques estão causando escassez do combustível que está “prejudicando o mundo”.
items.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, disse neste domingo ao presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, que pare de atacar a infraestrutura russa de diesel, afirmando que os ataques estão causando escassez do combustível que está “prejudicando o mundo”.
Uma onda de ataques ucranianos com drones de longo alcance contra refinarias de petróleo russas nos últimos meses reduziu a produção de combustível da Rússia, provocando escassez de gasolina em todo o território.
A Ucrânia, que enfrenta ataques russos regulares à sua própria infraestrutura energética, afirma que as refinarias são alvos militares legítimos.
O preço médio nacional do diesel nos EUA — utilizado por caminhões, trens, navios e equipamentos agrícolas — ultrapassou US$6 por galão pela primeira vez na quinta-feira, de acordo com o site de acompanhamento de preços GasBuddy.
“O Sr. Zelenskiy precisa fazer uma coisa: ele precisa parar de destruir o estoque de diesel na Rússia”, disse Trump a jornalistas durante uma visita ao torneio de golfe Irish Open, que está sendo realizado no oeste da Irlanda, em um campo de golfe de propriedade de sua família.
“Conversamos com o Sr. Zelenskiy sobre isso. Há muitos outros alvos. Não atinjam o diesel. Isso está prejudicando o mundo”, disse ele.
A escassez global “não é causada pelo Oriente Médio, mas sim pelo que está acontecendo com a Rússia e a Ucrânia”, acrescentou Trump.
A Rússia reduziu sua previsão de produção de petróleo para este ano para o nível mais baixo em 17 anos e revisou suas perspectivas de exportação de combustível para 2026 e 2027 devido à guerra, de acordo com um rascunho de previsão do governo analisado pela Reuters.
(Reportagem de Bo Erickson)

items.title: Report: 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) out 1 month
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A non-contact left ankle injury in San Francisco's season-opening victory will keep 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling sidelined for at least a month, NFL Network reported Sunday.
items.body:
A non-contact left ankle injury in San Francisco's season-opening victory will keep 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling sidelined for at least a month, NFL Network reported Sunday.
Stribling was injured in the second quarter of the 49ers' 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday in Australia and did not return. According to the report, the injury is a deltoid ligament sprain.
The former Ole Miss star might need to have surgery, per the report, but it had not been determined as of Sunday morning.
After the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan said that the rookie's Achilles was intact, but that more tests were required to determine the exact nature of the injury.
The 49ers chose Stribling, 23, with the first pick of the second round (No. 33 overall) in the 2026 NFL Draft. The Hawaii native earned more playing time after impressing the team at training camp.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Rusia ataca un tren de pasajeros en frontera de Ucrania con Polonia, no alcanza a "tren diplomático"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Un dron ruso impactó el domingo contra un tren de pasajeros en la frontera de Ucrania con Polonia, país miembro de la OTAN, poco después de que el ex primer ministro británico Boris Johnson y otros diplomáticos europeos utilizaron la misma línea.
items.body:
Un dron ruso impactó el domingo contra un tren de pasajeros en la frontera de Ucrania con Polonia, país miembro de la OTAN, poco después de que el ex primer ministro británico Boris Johnson y otros diplomáticos europeos utilizaron la misma línea.
El tren, que circulaba por una ruta muy utilizada por las delegaciones extranjeras que regresan de Kiev, fue atacado a solo 2 kilómetros (1,2 millas) de la frontera polaca, informó la empresa ferroviaria ucraniana.
No se han registrado víctimas.
"No era nuestro tren, sino el que iba unos minutos detrás de nosotros por el paso fronterizo. Se evacuó cuando se acercó el dron y nadie resultó herido", dijo Carl Bildt, ex primer ministro de Suecia, en X.
Él y otros políticos regresaban a Europa en tren tras asistir a una conferencia en Kiev.
"Es muy posible que el objetivo del dron ruso fuera el tren diplomático, que salió de la estación antes de lo previsto tras ajustarse los horarios de los trenes en tiempo real debido a la amenaza constante de ataques rusos", dijo en Telegram la empresa ferroviaria ucraniana, Ukrzaliznytsia.
Boris Johnson, que también se encontraba en el tren que salió de la estación poco antes del ataque, condenó este como "aleatorio y sin sentido" en una publicación en Instagram.
Dado que la línea del frente se mantiene prácticamente estática, tanto Moscú como Kiev han intensificado los ataques a larga distancia en las últimas semanas para intentar cambiar el rumbo de la guerra.
El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores polaco, Radoslaw Sikorski, calificó los crecientes ataques de Rusia a las puertas de la OTAN como "una escalada".
El domingo por la mañana, un camión situado a menos de 1 km de la frontera de Ucrania con Polonia también fue alcanzado, lo que provocó que el paso fronterizo de Dorohusk-Yahodyn suspendiera brevemente sus operaciones, según los guardias fronterizos.
El Ministerio de Defensa ruso dijo que había atacado infraestructuras que facilitaban el transporte de cargamentos militares procedentes de Europa en el oeste de Ucrania.
Rusia ha comenzado a atacar en las últimas semanas los pasos fronterizos de Ucrania con sus aliados occidentales, como parte de una campaña cada vez más intensa por ambas partes para debilitar la infraestructura económica del adversario, cuando ya se han cumplido más de cuatro años desde el inicio de la invasión rusa.
RUSIA REPORTA ATAQUE CERCA DE CENTRAL NUCLEAR DE ZAPORIYIA Durante la noche, las hostilidades no dieron señales de amainar.
En la parte controlada por Rusia de la región de Zaporiyia, al sureste de Ucrania, el director de Rosatom, la empresa estatal rusa de energía nuclear, acusó a Ucrania de atacar camiones de combustible cerca de la central nuclear de Zaporiyia, la mayor de Europa.
La central nuclear de Zaporiyia está bajo control ruso desde marzo de 2022 y sigue situada cerca de la línea del frente. Un portavoz militar ucraniano no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.
En la propia Rusia, el alcalde de la ciudad de Nizhnekamsk, en la región del río Volga, en Tartaristán, afirmó que objetivos "civiles e industriales" de la ciudad habían sido atacados por drones ucranianos, lo que provocó al menos dos muertos y varios heridos más.
El alcalde, Radmir Belyaev, no aclaró qué objetivos habían sido alcanzados, pero la ciudad alberga una importante refinería de petróleo que ya ha sido objeto de ataques en el pasado.
Las autoridades ucranianas no se pronunciaron de inmediato sobre el ataque a Nizhnekamsk, pero sí dijeron que habían atacado otra refinería en la región meridional de Krasnodar.

items.title: Team Europe jolts Americans, reclaims Solheim Cup
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Team Europe regained the Solheim Cup with a 15-13 victory over the United States on Sunday in Den Bosch, Netherlands.
items.body:
Team Europe regained the Solheim Cup with a 15-13 victory over the United States on Sunday in Den Bosch, Netherlands.
Lottie Woad sank a 2-foot putt on the 17th hole to record a 2&1 win over Auston Kim, pushing the Europeans past the 14 1/2-point threshold at Bernardus Golf. That included Carlota Ciganda's guaranteed half point in her match.
The successful putt ignited a celebration that featured Woad leaping into the arms of her teammates as Europe reveled in its eighth win in the event and avenged the United States' victory in 2024.
Woad admitted she wasn't sure if it was her match or that of Carlota Ciganda that ultimately would cement the victory for Team Europe.
"I knew it was mine or Carlota's match," Woad said. "And when Auston made those three birdies in a row that was great golf from her and I just had to try and stay steady, and the moment on 16 was a key one, definitely."
Ciganda sealed the win with a 4-and-2 victory over Jennifer Kupcho, who sank a 93-foot putt to upend Ciganda on Saturday.
"I think it's been one of the best teams that we've had in the last few years," Ciganda said. "Everyone is just a unit, a team. That's what Europe is about."
The teams were locked in an 8-8 tie before Europe bolted out of the blocks by winning six of Sunday's first eight matches, save for Alison Lee rallying from four down after 11 holes to notch a 1 up win over Esther Henseleit.
That represented the biggest comeback in a singles competition in Solheim Cup history.
"Huge," Lee said of securing the victory. "I definitely kept an eye on the leaderboard the whole round. I did see a lot of blue up there, but I just did the best I can to change mine red and thankfully I was able to pull it off."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Trump reiterates support for united Ireland, says won't talk about Scotland 'yet'
items.author: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday reiterated his support for Northern Ireland breaking from the United Kingdom to unify with the Republic of Ireland, but said he would not talk about Scotland becoming independent "yet".
items.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday reiterated his support for Northern Ireland breaking from the United Kingdom to unify with the Republic of Ireland, but said he would not talk about Scotland becoming independent "yet".
Trump surprised officials in Dublin and annoyed pro-British politicians in Northern Ireland and London by enthusiastically[USN:L6N454021 TEXT:" backing"] Irish unity during a visit to Dublin on Saturday, saying he would "love" to see it happen sooner rather than later.
"You have Northern Ireland and you have Ireland and it would seem to me that one of the 'naturals' of all time is to put them together," Trump told reporters during a visit to a golf tournament at one of his resorts, doubling down on his initial comments.
"You asked about Scotland. That one I won't talk about yet. I'll save that for another day," he added.
Scotland, where the Trump family also owns a golf resort, voted against independence from the rest of Britain in 2014. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has [USN:SPN43N00V TEXT:"ruled out"] another vote, as well as a referendum on Northern Ireland leaving the UK.
Trump made his comments about Irish unity after a meeting with Micheal Martin, the country's prime minister. In his first comments since Trump's remarks, the Irish premier said the response from some unionist politicians was "an overreaction".
"It shouldn't be a surprise. He takes a different sort of perspective on things," Martin told reporters on Sunday after meeting Trump again for lunch at the golf course.
Martin said the pair discussed Northern Ireland and its relationship with the Republic of Ireland and that he also went through with the president how the British-run region achieved peace.
A 1998 peace agreement ended three decades of violence between Irish nationalists seeking a united Ireland and unionists who wanted Northern Ireland to remain part of the UK.
"I support unity, I don't see it happening now. I've been very clear about that," Martin told BBC News in a separate interview.
"The chances are if one (vote) was held next week, it would find great difficulty in getting through."

items.title: Un ataque israelí mata a dos personas en Gaza, informan servicios médicos
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Un ataque aéreo israelí perpetrado el domingo causó la muerte de al menos dos palestinos que viajaban en un vehículo e hirió a otros 13 en la Franja de Gaza, informó personal médico.
items.body:
Un ataque aéreo israelí perpetrado el domingo causó la muerte de al menos dos palestinos que viajaban en un vehículo e hirió a otros 13 en la Franja de Gaza, informó personal médico.
El ataque, perpetrado en el barrio de Tel Al-Hawa, al oeste de la ciudad de Gaza, dejó el vehículo destrozado, según las imágenes difundidas en las redes sociales.
El personal médico local dijo a Reuters que había instado a la población a facilitar información que pudiera ayudar a identificar a las dos personas fallecidas, cuyos cuerpos quedaron desmembrados por la explosión.
El Ejército israelí dijo que el ataque tenía como objetivo a dos militantes de Hamás, sin dar más detalles.
Un alto el fuego de octubre de 2025, respaldado por Estados Unidos, puso fin a los combates a gran escala en Gaza, pero no ha detenido los ataques israelíes y se ha avanzado muy poco en las medidas encaminadas a una paz permanente.
Hamás acusa a Israel de violar el alto el fuego y de socavar los esfuerzos para aplicar el plan más amplio del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, para poner fin al conflicto de Gaza, que incluye la retirada israelí de la Franja y el desarme de Hamás.
Israel dice que Hamás ha estado violando el acuerdo.
Más de 1.300 palestinos, en su mayoría civiles, han perdido la vida en Gaza desde que entró en vigor el alto el fuego, según las autoridades sanitarias del territorio, mientras que el Ejército israelí dice que han fallecido cuatro soldados israelíes.
Hamás no suele revelar información sobre las bajas entre sus combatientes.

items.summary: Israel and Lebanon will meet in Rome in October to discuss a U.S.-brokered security agreement intended to ease hostilities along the border, a State Department Official told Reuters.
items.body:
Israel and Lebanon will meet in Rome in October to discuss a U.S.-brokered security agreement intended to ease hostilities along the border, a State Department Official told Reuters.
The continued implementation of the deal “remains the only viable mechanism to restore Lebanon’s sovereignty and Israel’s security,” the official said, adding that the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors will meet in Washington next week.
The seventh round of negotiations in the Italian capital ended in August without a breakthrough on key territorial issues.
Hezbollah and Israel returned to war on March 2 amid the wider regional conflict .
Israel's military is occupying what it describes as a "buffer zone" about 10 km (6 miles) into Lebanon along the entire length of the Israeli border. Israeli officials say the zone is necessary to protect northern Israeli communities from attacks launched by Hezbollah.
More than 4,300 people have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon since March, according to Lebanon's health ministry.

items.title: Carney impulsa la idea de convertir a Canadá en "miembro asociado" de la UE, informa el WSJ
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El primer ministro de Canadá, Mark Carney, desea estrechar las relaciones con la Unión Europea y está estudiando si su país podría convertirse en "miembro asociado" del bloque, informó el domingo el Wall Street Journal.
items.body:
El primer ministro de Canadá, Mark Carney, desea estrechar las relaciones con la Unión Europea y está estudiando si su país podría convertirse en "miembro asociado" del bloque, informó el domingo el Wall Street Journal.
La UE, que en el pasado no se ha mostrado flexible en cuanto a las normas de adhesión, está abierta a la idea de conceder a Canadá un estatuto de miembro asociado aún por crear, informó el periódico, citando a funcionarios anónimos tanto de la UE como de Canadá.
La embajada de Canadá en Bruselas y los portavoces de la Comisión Europea no respondieron a las respectivas solicitudes de comentarios.
La escalada de la guerra comercial de Canadá con Estados Unidos ha añadido urgencia a su giro estratégico hacia otros socios comerciales.
Las relaciones entre Ottawa y Washington se han deteriorado considerablemente desde que el presidente Donald Trump regresó a la Casa Blanca el año pasado debido a desacuerdos sobre el comercio y otras cuestiones. La disputa comercial ha dado lugar a aranceles que afectan a decenas de miles de millones de dólares en comercio transfronterizo.
Canadá y la UE están debatiendo formas de permitir que los bienes, servicios y trabajadores canadienses que participan en cadenas de suministro estratégicas —como la energía, la inteligencia artificial, la defensa y los minerales críticos— puedan circular libremente, desplazando así de manera efectiva la frontera de la UE, informó el Wall Street Journal.
Canadá y la UE también están hablando de tender cables submarinos, construir conjuntamente centros de datos, almacenamiento en la nube y nuevas redes de satélites, así como infraestructuras para transportar energía canadiense a la UE, según el periódico.
Carney ha mantenido conversaciones periódicas con varios líderes de la UE, entre los que destaca el presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, sobre la posibilidad de permitir que los canadienses vivan y trabajen en la UE sin necesidad de visado, según el WSJ, que cita a dos funcionarios anónimos familiarizados con el asunto.
La oficina de prensa de Macron no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios.
La oficina de Macron confirmó por separado que se reunirá con Carney el 20 de septiembre en el territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón, un archipiélago situado frente a la costa atlántica de Canadá.
La reunión supone la primera visita oficial de un primer ministro canadiense al archipiélago y "simboliza la solidez de la relación que une a nuestros dos países", señaló el Elíseo.
Sin embargo, cualquier proyecto destinado a estrechar los lazos entre Canadá y la UE probablemente se enfrentará a dificultades, a juzgar por los esfuerzos realizados en el pasado para poner en marcha un acuerdo comercial más modesto, que se ha topado con una feroz oposición dentro de Europa.
Más de una década después de que se alcanzó el acuerdo y nueve años desde su entrada en vigor provisional, varios países de la UE aún no lo han ratificado.

items.title: Doblete de Lamine Yamal ayuda al Barcelona a vencer al Levante
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lamine Yamal marcó dos goles y el Barcelona siguió con su inicio perfecto de temporada tras imponerse por 4-2 al Levante en un reñido partido de LaLiga de fútbol de España disputado el domingo en Valencia.
items.body:
Lamine Yamal marcó dos goles y el Barcelona siguió con su inicio perfecto de temporada tras imponerse por 4-2 al Levante en un reñido partido de LaLiga de fútbol de España disputado el domingo en Valencia.
Xavi Espart y Karim Adeyemi también marcaron para el Barcelona, que se sitúa en solitario en lo más alto de la clasificación de LaLiga con cinco victorias en cinco partidos, tres puntos por delante del Real Madrid.
El Barcelona se adelantó a los cinco minutos, cuando una hábil jugada a un toque terminó con un disparo de Espart, de 19 años, desde el borde del área que, tras un ligero desvío, se coló en la portería, suponiendo su primer gol en la categoría absoluta.
El Barcelona siguió dominando la posesión y aumentó su ventaja en el minuto 19. Raphinha controló con maestría un pase en profundidad de Fermín López y encontró a Lamine, desmarcado en el centro del área, para que rematara a puerta sin problemas.
El Levante se repuso tras sus dificultades iniciales, ejerciendo a su vez cierta presión, y, a pesar de no crear ocasiones claras, terminó la primera parte con seis disparos a puerta frente a los tres del Barcelona.
Gerard Martín, que cojeaba, fue blanco de los delanteros del Levante, y el entrenador del Barcelona, Hansi Flick, lo sustituyó en el descanso por Andreas Christensen.
Aissa Mandi cometió un penal a Lamine a los 42 segundos de la reanudación. El extremo culé marcó el lanzamiento desde los 12 pasos para completar su tercer doblete en tres partidos de LaLiga y frustrar la creciente confianza del Levante en que podía remontar el partido.
El Levante estuvo a punto de marcar a la hora de juego, cuando Víctor García superó al portero Joan García, pero un bloqueo parcial de Pau Cubarsi y un despeje de Christensen sobre la línea de gol se combinaron para evitar el gol.
Un pase erróneo de Espart en el minuto 79 permitió al Levante recortar distancias: el delantero Iván Romero regateó a Joan García antes de enviar el balón al fondo de la red.
Nueve minutos más tarde, Roger Brugue se abrió paso entre varias entradas del Barcelona para reducir la diferencia a un solo gol, en un momento en que lo que parecía una cómoda victoria del Barcelona amenazaba con convertirse en una heroica remontada del Levante.
Sin embargo, una carrera de Adeyemi y su inteligente remate en el minuto 93 acabaron con las esperanzas de los locales de conseguir el empate. No obstante, la afición local mostró su reconocimiento por el espíritu de lucha demostrado por su equipo, coreando "Levante" mientras el alemán celebraba su gol.
A pesar de su tropiezo en los últimos compases, el Barcelona se aseguró su sexta victoria consecutiva en todas las competencias, con la sólida actuación de Rodri en el centro del campo y el incansable esfuerzo del capitán Raphinha como piezas clave de su éxito.

items.title: Lamine Yamal double helps Barcelona beat Levante
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona continued their perfect start to the season.
items.body:
Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona continued their perfect start to the season with a hard-fought 4-2 LaLiga victory over Levante in Valencia on Sunday.
Xavi Espart and Karim Adeyemi were also on target for Barcelona, who are alone at the top of the LaLiga table with five wins from five, three points ahead of Real Madrid.
Barcelona went ahead after five minutes when a slick one-touch move ended with 19-year-old Espart firing home from the edge of the box via a slight deflection for his first senior goal.
Barcelona continued to dominate possession and doubled their advantage in the 19th minute. Raphinha controlled Fermin Lopez's through ball expertly and picked out an unmarked Lamine in the centre of the box for an easy finish.
Levante rallied after their early struggles, applying some pressure of their own, and despite failing to create a clear opening, ended the half with six attempts to Barcelona's three.
Gerard Martin, who appeared to be limping, was withdrawn by Barcelona manager Hansi Flick at halftime and replaced by Andreas Christensen.
Barcelona struck when Aissa Mandi conceded a penalty for a foul on Lamine 42 seconds after the restart. The winger converted the spot kick to complete his third double in as many LaLiga matches and puncture Levante's growing belief that they could fight their way back into the contest.
Levante came close on the hour when Victor Garcia beat goalkeeper Joan Garcia, but a partial block by Pau Cubarsi and Christensen's goal-line clearance combined to keep his effort out.
An errant pass from Espart in the 79th minute allowed Levante to pull one back, with forward Ivan Romero rounding Joan Garcia before passing the ball into the net.
Nine minutes later, Roger Brugue burst through multiple Barcelona challenges to reduce the deficit to one goal as what looked like a comfortable Barcelona win threatened to turn into a heroic Levante comeback.
Yet Adeyemi's mazy run and smart finish in the 93rd minute ended the hosts' hopes of a draw. The home crowd nevertheless showed their appreciation for the fighting spirit shown by their side, chanting 'Levante' as the German celebrated his goal.
Despite their late wobble, Barcelona secured a sixth successive win in all competitions, with Rodri's assured midfield display and captain Raphinha's relentless running central to their success.
ATLETICO LEAVE IT LATE Atletico Madrid scored three late goals to beat Real Sociedad 3-0, as new signings Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David scored their first goals since joining the club.
Both sides struggled to create clear chances until Grimaldo netted an 84th-minute penalty, before David doubled their lead after finding space on the break six minutes later.
Giuliano Simeone added a third in the 95th minute to complete the scoring for Atletico, who were without key players Julian Alvarez and Pablo Barrios due to muscle injuries as they returned to winning ways following two consecutive losses.

VALENCIA, Sept 13 : Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona continued their perfect start to the season with a hard-fought 4-2 LaLiga victory over Levante in Valencia on Sunday. 
Xavi Espart and Karim Adeyemi were also on target for Barcelona, who are alone at the top of the LaLiga table with five wins from five, three points ahead of Real Madrid.
Barcelona went ahead after five minutes when a slick one-touch move ended with 19-year-old Espart firing home from the edge of the box via a slight deflection for his first senior goal.
Barcelona continued to dominate possession and doubled their advantage in the 19th minute. Raphinha controlled Fermin Lopez's through ball expertly and picked out an unmarked Lamine in the centre of the box for an easy finish.

Levante rallied after their early struggles, applying some pressure of their own, and despite failing to create a clear opening, ended the half with six attempts to Barcelona's three.
Gerard Martin, who appeared to be limping, was withdrawn by Barcelona manager Hansi Flick at halftime and replaced by Andreas Christensen.
Barcelona struck when Aissa Mandi conceded a penalty for a foul on Lamine 42 seconds after the restart. The winger converted the spot kick to complete his third double in as many LaLiga matches and puncture Levante's growing belief that they could fight their way back into the contest.
Levante came close on the hour when Victor Garcia beat goalkeeper Joan Garcia, but a partial block by Pau Cubarsi and Christensen's goal-line clearance combined to keep his effort out.
An errant pass from Espart in the 79th minute allowed Levante to pull one back, with forward Ivan Romero rounding Joan Garcia before passing the ball into the net.
Nine minutes later, Roger Brugue burst through multiple Barcelona challenges to reduce the deficit to one goal as what looked like a comfortable Barcelona win threatened to turn into a heroic Levante comeback.
Yet Adeyemi's mazy run and smart finish in the 93rd minute ended the hosts' hopes of a draw. The home crowd nevertheless showed their appreciation for the fighting spirit shown by their side, chanting 'Levante' as the German celebrated his goal.
Despite their late wobble, Barcelona secured a sixth successive win in all competitions, with Rodri's assured midfield display and captain Raphinha's relentless running central to their success.
ATLETICO LEAVE IT LATE
Atletico Madrid scored three late goals to beat Real Sociedad 3-0, as new signings Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David scored their first goals since joining the club.
Both sides struggled to create clear chances until Grimaldo netted an 84th-minute penalty, before David doubled their lead after finding space on the break six minutes later.
Giuliano Simeone added a third in the 95th minute to complete the scoring for Atletico, who were without key players Julian Alvarez and Pablo Barrios due to muscle injuries as they returned to winning ways following two consecutive losses.
Malaga rescued a 1-1 draw against Celta Vigo, who had dominated the game at Balaidos, while Deportivo A Coruna also drew 1-1 with Getafe after going behind in the second half.

items.title: Trump calls $5,000 payouts 'easy' to fit into federal budget
items.author: Bo Erickson, Chuck Mikolajczak, Padraic Halpin
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Chuck Mikolajczak, Padraic Halpin
items.summary: Congress would have to approve such a payment, House Speaker Mike Johnson said.
items.body:
President Donald Trump said on Sunday the United States can afford his promise to send $5,000 to every U.S. adult should his Republican Party keep control of Congress in this year's elections.
"I don't know but it's easy if the Republicans win. $5,000 to all adults in the country and we can easily handle that because we're taking in so much money," Trump told reporters when asked if Congress would need to approve the payments, adding that trillions of dollars were coming into the country.
Trump unveiled the idea of $5,000 payouts [USN:L1N451146 TEXT:"during a speech"] at the Republican Party convention last week. Speaking to reporters on Sunday in Ireland, where he was attending a golf tournament at his club in Doonbeg, the president said the U.S. government has the funds to pay for it.
But any such payment would need to be approved by Congress, House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, said on Sunday. "Of course, the devil's in the details. We have to figure all that out," Johnson told CNN's "State of the Union."
Democratic politicians on Sunday morning talk shows panned the idea, with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries telling ABC's "This Week" that it is not a "serious proposal."
U.S. Senator Mallory McMorrow, citing [USN:L1N41O16Y TEXT:"the elimination of some Affordable Care Act subsidies"], cast doubt on whether the promised $5,000 checks would be sent even if Republicans retain control of Congress.
"There was an ACA subsidy cancellation," McMorrow, a Michigan Democrat, said on CNN. "I think it was $1,000 we were supposed to get. So if you believe that you're going to get $5,000, I've got a bridge to sell you."
U.S. Representative Mike Lawler, a New York Republican in a closely contested race, would not specifically commit to Trump’s $5,000 dividend proposal on Sunday.
“I support putting money back in the pockets of hardworking Americans,” he said on ABC’s “This Week,” citing tax cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill that Republicans passed last year.
“But whether you call it a stimulus check or a dividend, the question is, how do you pay for it? That's my focus. We have a $4 trillion debt, and we have to be serious about tackling that.”
Lisa Gilbert, co-president of the consumer watchdog Public Citizen, earlier called the move an attempt to buy votes.
"This explicit and desperate attempt to buy votes in the November election is a new low. Trump knows he can’t do this, and yet he’s attempting to bribe voters with the false promise of cash to help his party win an election, which is antithetical to every principle of American democracy."

DOONBEG, Ireland: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Sep 13) likened critics of artificial intelligence to "very negative forces" bringing up scenarios that will not happen, and said he wanted to make sure that the US remains the industry leader.
"We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins," Trump told reporters at his Ireland golf course, when asked if the AI industry should slow down or be more regulated.
"We could put guardrails. We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up, and they're bringing up things that won't happen."
Trump has resisted stirring concerns about AI.

The public debate about AI has heated up in the US after two Anthropic researchers issued warnings that the rapidly progressing technology could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future.
In his second term, Trump's administration has largely embraced AI firms. These AI leaders and other technology companies have also supported Trump's initiatives.
AI executives have poured money into the midterm campaign ahead of the Nov 3 election that will determine control of Congress. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's super PAC, America PAC, has already spent millions backing Republican candidates and is expected to play a major role in voter turnout efforts this fall.
The Pentagon this year warned of risks from Anthropic's model.
After the researchers' warnings, some AI CEOs are pushing for slowing advancement of the models.
On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a three-step framework intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks. The proposal immediately received endorsements from several other executives at major AI companies, including Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
In an interview that aired Sunday on the CBS program "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan", Amodei said the competition between US and Chinese AI companies was the "toughest dilemma" in trying to establish a "speed limit" on the rate of AI development.
"We shouldn't kid ourselves, because the incentives to pull ahead and the military advantage that you get from that are so large that the ability to check that the other side isn't cheating has to be ironclad," he said. "So I think that's going to be the work of years, and honestly, I don't know if it's possible."
Jacob Coxon, one of the Anthropic researchers who resigned and then issued the warnings, pushed for the US to work with other countries to ensure pace.
"I feel we need international coordination, or else we risk running the same race with China, which could be equally dangerous," Coxon said on NBC's Meet the Press.

Anthropic boss calls for AI slowdown, Altman and Musk agree

Commentary: Some Anthropic engineers think AI might end us. Why race ahead?

items.summary: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sat out Week 1 with a back injury amid an "impasse" between the fourth-year defensive back and Pittsburgh's front office in contract extension talks.
items.body:
Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sat out Week 1 with a back injury amid an "impasse" between the fourth-year defensive back and Pittsburgh's front office in contract extension talks.
Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Porter and the team have not been able to make progress on a long-term contract extension.
ESPN reported Sunday that the Steelers are "listening" to offers for Porter. He was listed as questionable this week.
Porter said at the end of training camp that he would consider not suiting up if the two sides didn't make some type of progress toward a new deal. Porter requested a trade and informed the team he is open to moving elsewhere, ESPN reported.
"I mean, at the end of the day, it's business, and I know what that is and I got my head straight to understand that," Porter said Friday.
Since the end of the 2025 regular season, four cornerbacks have signed contracts averaging at least $30 million annually.
Porter, the son of former Steelers outside linebacker Joey Porter Sr., was a second-round pick (No. 32 overall) in the 2023 draft. He has three career interceptions in 47 regular-season games.
--Field Level Media

items.title: ホルムズ巡るオマーンとの合意案、イランが14日に湾岸諸国に提示へ
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： イランは14日、ホルムズ海峡を通る暫定航路を巡るオマーンとの合意案を湾岸諸国に正式に提示する見通しだ。イランの大統領とアラブ首長国連邦（UAE）アブダビ首長国の皇太子が異例の会談を行うなど、背後では外交活動が活発化している。

事情に詳しい関係者によると、イランはオマーンと合意した新たな暫定航路の内容を湾岸諸国に示す予定だ。船舶に課す可能性がある通航料など詳細については、両国が今後も協議を続ける。非公開の協議内容だとして、関係者は匿名を条件に語った。

世界のエネルギー輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡を巡っては、イランとオマーンの協議がここ数週間で進展している。オマーンは14日、南部サラーラで湾岸協力会議（GCC）加盟国の外相会合を開くことを目指していた。

UAEアブダビ首長国のハリド皇太子は、インドで開かれた有力新興国グループ、BRICSの首脳会議に合わせ、イランのペゼシュキアン大統領と会談した。両国の高官が公の場で協議するのは異例。

イラン側はこれまで、合意が成立しても海峡の全面的な再開にはならず、どの船舶の通航を認めるかは引き続き自国が判断するとの考えを示している。同国のアラグチ外相は、予定されている会合は「重要な出来事」であり、信頼醸成に向けた一歩だと、アルアラビ・アルジャディードとのインタビューで述べた。

UAE国営のWAM通信によると、ハリド皇太子とペゼシュキアン氏は、緊張緩和を進め、地域の安定を強化する必要性を強調した。

UAEのアンワル・ガルガシュ大統領顧問はXへの投稿で、長引く危機の中でペゼシュキアン氏が「均衡の取れた合理的な」姿勢を示してきたと評価した。

UAEは今回の戦争でイランに対して強硬姿勢を取り、8月にはイランとの経済関係を正式に断絶した。一方で、政治的な解決も呼びかけている。

会合の参加国は明らかになっていない。バーレーンは、親イラン勢力による最近の湾岸地域への攻撃を理由に、参加しない意向を示している。サウジアラビアが支援する勢力と、隣国イエメンを拠点にイランの支援を受けるフーシ派との戦闘激化も、計画を複雑にする可能性がある。

items.title: Bloque de centroizquierda lidera elección en Suecia, muestran sondeos a boca de urna
items.author: Anna Ringstrom, Simon Johnson
items.creator: Anna Ringstrom, Simon Johnson
items.summary: Los partidos de centroizquierda de Suecia, que respaldan a la líder socialdemócrata Magdalena Andersson para el cargo de primera ministra, lideraban las elecciones parlamentarias celebradas el domingo con un 51,3% de los votos, según una encuesta a pie de urna realizada por la cadena SVT.
items.body:
Los partidos de centroizquierda de Suecia, que respaldan a la líder socialdemócrata Magdalena Andersson para el cargo de primera ministra, lideraban las elecciones parlamentarias celebradas el domingo con un 51,3% de los votos, según una encuesta a pie de urna realizada por la cadena SVT.
Se espera que la Autoridad Electoral sueca dé a conocer los primeros resultados en las próximas horas, tras el cierre de las urnas a las 20.00 hora local (1800 GMT). Otra encuesta realizada el mismo día de las elecciones por la cadena TV4 también situaba al centroizquierda en cabeza.
Si los resultados oficiales confirman la ventaja de la centroizquierda, esto frenaría el reciente giro hacia la derecha de Suecia, que la ha alejado de sus tradiciones liberales, en unas elecciones que muchos analistas consideraban un referéndum sobre los Demócratas de Suecia, una formación con raíces en la extrema derecha neonazi.
Las encuestas a boca de urna suecas, si bien a menudo son indicativas del resultado final, no siempre han resultado precisas. En 2022, una encuesta a pie de urna pronosticó que el bloque de Andersson se impondría, pero las elecciones las ganó finalmente una coalición de derecha encabezada por Ulf Kristersson, que ahora es primer ministro de Suecia.
A medida que se emitían los resultados de las encuestas a boca de urna, estallaron vítores en los mítines electorales de los partidos de centroizquierda, mientras que el resultado fue recibido con silencio entre los Demócratas de Suecia, de extrema derecha, ya que esos sondeos indicaban un revés tras haber aumentado su porcentaje de votos en varias elecciones consecutivas.
"Si esto se confirma, Magdalena Andersson se convertirá en la primera ministra de nuestro país", dijo el secretario del Partido Socialdemócrata, Tobias Baudin, a la SVT tras el anuncio de los resultados de la encuesta a boca de urna.
La encuesta a pie de urna de la SVT otorgaba al bloque de centroizquierda 183 escaños, por encima de los 175 necesarios para obtener la mayoría, mientras que los partidos de derecha se encaminaban a obtener 166 escaños.
"Existe un deseo de cambio", dijo Marie Demker, profesora de ciencias políticas de la Universidad de Gotemburgo. "Cómo se va a llevar a cabo ese cambio con las diferentes líneas rojas que han trazado estos partidos es una preocupación para mañana".
Muchos suecos han expresado su recelo ante la apuesta de Kristersson por imponer límites estrictos a la inmigración y consideraron que su promesa preelectoral de incorporar a los Demócratas de Suecia al Gobierno era ir demasiado lejos.
"Esto no es lo que esperábamos, pero no son los resultados definitivos, así que habrá que esperar", dijo a TV4 el vicepresidente del partido Demócratas de Suecia, Henrik Vinge.
"Es habitual que se produzca un cierto descenso cuando se forma parte de la coalición de gobierno", añadió.
Kristersson, que se ha mantenido a la zaga en las encuestas de opinión a lo largo de sus cuatro años en el cargo, había ido recortando distancias en las últimas semanas de campaña, mientras que Andersson y sus socialdemócratas perdían terreno.
Los críticos afirman que el Gobierno de Kristersson está socavando las libertades civiles, al tiempo que obliga a los inmigrantes a adaptarse más estrictamente a las normas culturales suecas o a abandonar el país, mediante incentivos y sanciones.
El éxito electoral de los Demócratas de Suecia sería bien recibido por los partidos de extrema derecha en auge en Europa, que se vieron reforzados por la victoria del partido antiinmigrante Alternativa para Alemania en unas elecciones regionales celebradas la semana pasada en Alemania.
La extrema derecha espera obtener avances en las próximas elecciones en toda Europa, siendo la candidatura de Agrupación Nacional a la presidencia francesa del año que viene, potencialmente, su mayor premio.

items.title: No luck for Norris as Antonelli becomes Madring's first F1 winner
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: Mercedes's Kimi Antonelli won the first Spanish Grand Prix held at Madrid's new circuit to take another huge stride towards the Formula One title after bad luck denied Lando Norris victory for McLaren on Sunday.
items.body:
Mercedes's Kimi Antonelli won the first Spanish Grand Prix held at Madrid's new circuit to take another huge stride towards the Formula One title after bad luck denied Lando Norris victory for McLaren on Sunday.
The 20-year-old Italian's triumph from starting second on the grid at the Madring was his eighth win of the season and stretched his championship lead over teammate George Russell to 81 points after 14 rounds.
Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen was second with reigning champion Norris third. Russell finished fifth.
"I think today it's good to win but it doesn't feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win but overall, we take it," said Antonelli.
VIRTUAL SAFETY CAR PROVES DECISIVE Antonelli benefited from a virtual safety car (VSC) on lap 15 falling at just the right time for him to come in for a change of tyres and too late for McLaren's pole-sitter Norris, who was leading and had already gone past the pit entrance seconds earlier.
When Norris came in at the next opportunity, on lap 16 of 57, the race had gone green again.
The pitstop was slow, due to a problem on the front right of the car, but McLaren and Pirelli said that made little difference and the damage had already been done on a track that lived up to fears it would be impossible to overtake.
Norris said there was nothing he could do, with all the top three on the same one-stop strategy.
"I felt like we deserved it today but that's racing sometimes," he said. "I feel like I drove a perfect race today, just luck wasn't with me.
"It's just incredibly frustrating to lose in a way that has nothing to do with performance."
OPENING BATTLE BETWEEN ANTONELLI AND NORRIS Antonelli twice had to give the lead back to Norris on the opening lap after cutting corners and gaining an advantage while trying to pass but the Briton then settled into a rhythm and began to pull away.
Verstappen also gained places that he had to hand back to Antonelli and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, despite complaining that the latter had "almost shunted into me" and was out of control.
Hamilton then suffered a brake problem that sent him plunging down the order and the seven-time world champion was eventually forced to retire.
Norris was more than six seconds clear with everything seemingly under control when Aston Martin's Lance Stroll triggered the VSC by stopping at turn 20.
Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell all pitted, saving precious seconds compared to a normal stop.
When Norris came in for a switch to hard tyres to take him to the end of the race, he was stationary for seven seconds and returned to the track in fifth place but effectively fourth with Ferrari's new leader Charles Leclerc yet to stop.
Leclerc stayed out until lap 48, hoping in vain for another safety car to give him a cheap stop, and then pitted. He ended up fourth.
The virtual safety car proved decisive, with the remainder of the afternoon effectively a high-speed procession to the chequered flag without major incident -- despite fears that there could be multiple crashes and red flags as seen in earlier junior races -- or much to get excited about.
Antonelli crossed the line 4.3 seconds clear of Verstappen with Norris a further 0.7 behind, pushing hard but with no way past.
"Of course we know that Lando got unlucky with that VSC, so for us I think today P2 is an incredible result because you could see how much Lando was catching me," said Verstappen.
Liam Lawson, standing in for the injured Isack Hadjar for the third race in a row, was sixth for Red Bull with Franco Colapinto seventh for Renault-owned Alpine and Oscar Piastri eighth in a damaged McLaren.
Arvid Lindblad secured precious points for Racing Bulls in their battle for fifth with Alpine and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg the final scorer in 10th.
Mercedes now have 503 points to Ferrari's 358 and McLaren's 306.
The next race is the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku on September 26.

items.title: Trump tells Ukraine's Zelenskiy to stop hitting Russian diesel
items.author: Bo Erickson
items.creator: Bo Erickson
items.summary: Long-distance Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries in recent months have reduced that country's fuel production, triggering gasoline shortages across the country.
items.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, saying the attacks were causing a shortage of the fuel that is "hurting the world".
A wave of long-distance Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries in recent months has reduced that country's fuel production, triggering gasoline shortages across the country.
Ukraine, which faces regular Russian attacks on its own energy infrastructure, says refineries are legitimate military targets.
The U.S. national average price for diesel, which is used by trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment, [USN:L6N4521A4 TEXT:"rose over $6"] a gallon for the first time on Thursday, according to price tracker GasBuddy.
"Mr. Zelenskiy has to do one thing: He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told journalists during a visit to the Irish Open, which is being held in the west of Ireland on a golf course owned by his family.
"We spoke to Mr. Zelenskiy about it. There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel. That's hurting the world," he said.
The global shortage "isn't done by the Middle East, this is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine," Trump added.
Russia [USN:L8N44P12J TEXT:"downgraded"] its oil output forecast for this year to a 17-year low and revised its fuel exports outlook for 2026 and 2027 due to the war, according to a government draft forecast seen by Reuters.

items.title: Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans after 'Jota' chants aimed at Neves
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo said on Sunday that fans who appeared to make chants referencing former teammate Diogo Jota at Ruben Neves during a Saudi Pro League match should be banned from football stadiums for life.
items.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo said on Sunday that fans who appeared to make chants referencing former teammate Diogo Jota at Ruben Neves during a Saudi Pro League match should be banned from football stadiums for life.
The chants occurred on Saturday during a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves' side Al-Hilal in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia.
[USN:S8N3QE0AD TEXT:"Jota died on July 3, 2025"], in a car crash in Zamora, northwestern Spain, along with his brother Andre Silva. A close friend of Jota, [USN:L4N3T2013 TEXT:"Neves was a pallbearer"] at his funeral.
Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting 'Jota'.
The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and then up to the sky in response.
Passing through the mixed zone after the game, Neves commented, "I hope they don't go to pray afterwards."
In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account.
"The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour," said Ronaldo.
"This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again."
The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.
Al-Hilal Club Company announced in a statement on their website on Sunday that they had filed a complaint with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation relating to the incident. The Saudi Pro League club were "confident" that measures would be taken to "protect the integrity of sporting competition from offensive practices."
"The Company expressed its absolute rejection of such actions targeting players or their families, or intended to cause personal offence," said Al-Hilal's statement.
Later on Sunday, Al-Taawoun also released a statement regarding the incident, which strongly condemned the offensive chants.
"Such conduct is completely unacceptable and does not represent Al-Taawoun, its supporters or the values for which its terraces are known."
Al-Taawoun say they will "take all necessary measures in coordination with the relevant authorities to prevent a recurrence and hold offenders accountable."

items.title: How Will Silicon Valley Rearm America?
items.summary: War in Ukraine, conflict in the Middle East and the rise of China have pushed national security back to the center of US economic and industrial strategy. Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper says the country needs to spend more on defense and better use cutting-edge weapons coming out of places like Silicon Valley, Austin and Boston. The opportunity is particularly striking in space, where companies like Apex Space are trying to industrialize satellite production as the US considers ambitious projects like Golden Dome . But the new defense-tech boom still faces hard questions: will the Pentagon procure quickly enough; will startups scale production; is space-based missile defense technically and financially realistic; and will the future belong to startups, legacy primes, or a marriage between the two? (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: 1 Nuevos ataques en Ormuz y Arabia Saudita arriesgan agravar perturbaciones en mercado petrolero
items.author: Mohammed Ghobari, Nayera Abdallah
items.creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Nayera Abdallah
items.summary: Los nuevos ataques contra Arabia Saudita y contra buques en el golfo Pérsico pusieron a prueba los ánimos en Oriente Medio el domingo, después de que un ataque contra un oleoducto saudí y un avance de los hutíes de Yemen amenazaron con agravar las perturbaciones del suministro energético mundial provocadas por la guerra.
items.body:
Los nuevos ataques contra Arabia Saudita y contra buques en el golfo Pérsico pusieron a prueba los ánimos en Oriente Medio el domingo, después de que un ataque contra un oleoducto saudí y un avance de los hutíes de Yemen amenazaron con agravar las perturbaciones del suministro energético mundial provocadas por la guerra.
Los operadores petroleros esperaban que los precios volvieran a subir cuando los mercados reabrieran el lunes, tras los acontecimientos del fin de semana que ponen en peligro el suministro del mayor exportador mundial, Arabia Saudita.
La agencia británica de seguridad marítima UKMTO informó el domingo de que un buque había sido alcanzado por un proyectil mientras atravesaba el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que provocó un incendio y obligó a evacuar a la tripulación.
Irán, por su parte, dijo que una persona había fallecido y cuatro tripulantes habían resultado heridos a bordo de un buque comercial iraní alcanzado frente a sus costas.
En Arabia Saudita, los medios de comunicación estatales difundieron un video de los daños sufridos por viviendas y una mezquita a causa del supuesto último ataque transfronterizo de los hutíes, en la provincia de Jazan, al sur del país. Por otra parte, los hutíes dijeron que atacaron una base militar saudí en una provincia vecina.
Las ciudades del sur de Arabia Saudita han sufrido alertas constantes desde la semana pasada, que culminaron el viernes con ataques con drones que inutilizaron el oleoducto de 1.200 km (745 millas) que atraviesa la península Arábiga de este a oeste y que ha servido como ruta principal para el suministro mundial de petróleo de Oriente Medio, evitando el estrecho de Ormuz.
Ese mismo día, los hutíes tomaron la isla de Perim, situada en medio de Bab el-Mandeb, el estrecho conocido como la "Puerta de las Lágrimas" que controla la desembocadura del mar Rojo.
EL PRECIO DEL DIÉSEL EN EEUU ALCANZA OTRO RÉCORD Los precios del petróleo superaron los 100 dólares esta semana por primera vez desde julio. El precio al por menor del diésel en Estados Unidos, un tema políticamente delicado, subió el domingo hasta alcanzar otro máximo histórico por encima de los 6,20 dólares el galón.
Los operadores y los compradores de petróleo saudíes dijeron el domingo a Reuters que Riad tiene suficientes reservas de petróleo en su puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo, para mantener las exportaciones durante solo entre cinco y siete días si el oleoducto afectado el viernes permanece cerrado.
A partir de entonces, podría verse comprometido hasta un 4% del suministro mundial de crudo, además de los millones de barriles diarios que ya se han perdido debido a la interrupción del tráfico a través del estrecho de Ormuz.
Arabia Saudita no ha facilitado detalles completos sobre la magnitud de los daños en el oleoducto ni ha indicado cuánto tiempo permanecerá fuera de servicio.
Las fuentes que han hablado con Reuters han ofrecido estimaciones contradictorias sobre el tiempo necesario para repararlo, que oscilan entre días y semanas. Las imágenes por satélite han mostrado enormes columnas de humo procedentes de distintos puntos a lo largo del oleoducto.
APLAZAN NEGOCIACIONES EN OMÁN Tras un agosto tranquilo en el que los flujos de petróleo de Oriente Medio se recuperaron poco a poco, las últimas dos semanas han sido testigo de una escalada constante en la guerra que Estados Unidos e Israel iniciaron hace seis meses.
No se han celebrado conversaciones de paz desde que un acuerdo provisional alcanzado en junio se vino abajo al cabo de unas semanas.
En una inusual iniciativa diplomática, funcionarios iraníes dijeron que asistirían el lunes a una reunión con los Estados árabes del Golfo en Omán para presentar un acuerdo que, según ellos, se había alcanzado con Omán y que regulaba las futuras rutas marítimas a través del estrecho.
Sin embargo, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Omán, Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, publicó el domingo por la noche que la reunión regional se había pospuesto "en aras del consenso".
"Seguimos comprometidos con el fomento del diálogo que respalde la estabilidad y la cooperación duradera en nuestra región", escribió en una publicación en X.
La agencia de noticias iraní Fars citó el domingo por la noche a un funcionario del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores iraní, quien dijo que la reunión de Omán se había pospuesto a petición de algunos países de la región, en una decisión tomada conjuntamente por Teherán y Mascate.
El funcionario señaló que Irán se coordinaría con Omán para fijar una fecha adecuada para celebrar la reunión, informó la agencia.
Irak había anunciado que enviaría una delegación, y un funcionario del Golfo había dicho a Reuters que Arabia Saudita y Qatar estarían representados por sus ministros de Asuntos Exteriores.
Un funcionario iraní de alto rango había dicho a Reuters el sábado que en la reunión se debatirían el estrecho de Ormuz y otras cuestiones, pero añadió que probablemente no se llegaría a firmar ningún acuerdo para reabrir el estrecho. Baréin dijo que no se reuniría con ningún representante iraní.
En una entrevista con el medio de comunicación panárabe con sede en Londres Al-Arabi Al-Jadeed, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán, Abbas Araqchi, dijo que, independientemente de cualquier acuerdo con Omán, Irán no reabriría el estrecho hasta que Estados Unidos satisficiera las exigencias de Teherán.
AVANCES DE LOS HUTÍ PLANTEAN UN NUEVO DILEMA PARA WASHINGTON Hasta ahora, Estados Unidos no ha logrado los objetivos que el presidente Donald Trump se fijó cuando puso en marcha la "Operación Epic Fury" en febrero: poner fin al programa nuclear de Irán, impedir que pueda atacar a sus vecinos y crear las condiciones para que su pueblo derroque a sus gobernantes.
Irán, que ha resistido la embestida de la superpotencia a pesar de las pérdidas militares y económicas, espera salir más fuerte que antes de la guerra, entre otras cosas gracias a la nueva facultad de cobrar tasas a los barcos que utilizan el estrecho.
Los ataques contra Arabia Saudita y los avances de los hutíes en Yemen plantean un nuevo dilema a Washington, que quiere apoyar a sus aliados saudíes y proteger el tráfico marítimo, pero se muestra reacio a sumarse a la guerra en otro frente.
Los ataques hutíes también han dejado a los Estados del Golfo ante una difícil elección: aceptar un creciente sufrimiento económico o entablar relaciones con Irán.
Los hutíes, combatientes de montaña que tomaron la capital de Yemen en 2014, llevan más de una década luchando contra una coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita, pero hasta hace unas semanas se habían mantenido en gran medida al margen de la guerra más amplia en Oriente Medio. Su avance a lo largo de la costa del mar Rojo forma parte del mayor recrudecimiento de los combates en Yemen en años.
Estados Unidos bombardeó a los hutíes durante dos meses en 2025, pero Trump detuvo esa campaña tras anunciar que el grupo había retirado la amenaza de atacar el tráfico marítimo del mar Rojo.
Tres fuentes informaron a Reuters de que el líder de facto de Arabia Saudita, el príncipe heredero Mohammed bin Salman, llamó por teléfono a Trump el jueves para solicitar ayuda militar para combatir a los hutíes, pero por el momento solo se le ofreció apoyo en materia de inteligencia.
Trump reconoció el sábado que había hablado con el príncipe heredero y dijo que los hutíes también habían llamado a la Administración estadounidense para pedir a Washington que se mantuviera al margen de la guerra de Yemen.

items.title: Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which has been used to reroute around 4 million barrels per day to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, was shut on Friday following drone attacks.

Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply

Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which has been used to reroute around 4 million barrels per day to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, was shut on Friday following drone attacks.

Trucks explode as they burn during what the Houthis say was an attack targeting trucks coming from Saudi territory at Al-Wadiah border crossing near Al-Wadiah, on the Saudi-Yemen border, in this still image obtained from a handout video released on Sep 7, 2026. (Image: Reuters/Houthi Media Centre)

LONDON: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it does not restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4 per cent of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said.
A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent US bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis.
Since drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its huge east-west oil pipeline on Friday (Sep 11), Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay offline.
Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing.

Saudi Arabia's government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
For the past six months, the pipeline running through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula has spared Saudi Arabia from the brunt of the impact of the wartime shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz that has crippled exports from its neighbours.
The world's biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day - around 4 per cent of global supply - to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea.
But with the pipeline out of service, Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days, according to three industry sources familiar with Saudi exports. Saudi Arabia also has stocks to supply customers for several days from Egypt's ports of Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, a fourth source said.
Yanbu storage capacity stands at around 35 million barrels, according to industry estimates, with Ain Sukhna and Sidi Kerir able to store 18 million and 20 million barrels respectively.
Stocks are not full and will ultimately run out without the east-west pipeline resuming operations, the four sources said.

Related:

Iran, Saudi Arabia discuss regional 'insecurity' as Yemen fighting flares

CNA Explains: With the Houthis' Red Sea threat, is the world running out of detours?

Saudi oil supply has already fallen to a more than three-decade low in August on reduced flows via Hormuz and the Red Sea, the International Energy Agency said on Friday. 
World oil supply will decline this year by 5.7 million barrels per day, or about 6 per cent, the IEA, which coordinates Western energy policies, said. In addition to the attack on the pipeline, Houthi fighters in Yemen, who have threatened Saudi oil shipments, seized an island on Friday in the mouth of the Red Sea.
The Middle East supplied around 22 million barrels per day of oil before the war. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz have slowed to just 6 million to 9 million bpd, industry sources say.
Saudi Arabia told OPEC last week that its oil production had dropped to just 6.2 million barrels per day in August from 10.9 million barrels per day in February before the start of the war.

items.title: Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply
items.author: Alex Lawler, Dmitry Zhdannikov
items.creator: Alex Lawler, Dmitry Zhdannikov
items.summary: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, Saudi oil buyers and traders said.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said.
A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent U.S. bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis.
Since drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to [USN:S8N44107L TEXT:"shut"] its huge east-west oil pipeline on Friday, Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay off-line.
Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing.
Saudi Arabia's government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
For the past six months, the pipeline running through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula has spared Saudi Arabia from the brunt of the impact of the wartime shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz that has crippled exports from its neighbours.
The world's biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around 4% of global supply — to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea.
But with the pipeline out of service, Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days, according to three industry sources familiar with Saudi exports.
Saudi Arabia also has stocks to supply customers for several days from Egypt's ports of Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, a fourth source said.
Yanbu storage capacity stands at around 35 million barrels, according to industry estimates, with Ain Sukhna and Sidi Kerir able to store 18 million and 20 million barrels respectively.
Stocks are not full and will ultimately run out without the east-west pipeline resuming operations, the four sources said.
Saudi oil supply has already fallen to a more than [USN:L6N4530LR TEXT:"three-decade low"] in August on reduced flows via Hormuz and the Red Sea, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.
World oil supply will [USN:L6N4530I5 TEXT:"decline"] this year by 5.7 million bpd, or about 6%, the IEA, which coordinates Western energy policies, said.In addition to the attack on the pipeline, Houthi fighters in Yemen who have threatened Saudi oil shipments seized an island on Friday in the mouth of the Red Sea .
The Middle East supplied around 22 million barrels per day of oil before the war. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz have slowed to just 6 million to 9 million bpd, industry sources say.
Saudi Arabia told OPEC last week that its oil production had dropped to just 6.2 million bpd in August from 10.9 million bpd in February before the start of the war.

items.title: AI企業トップの警告、目先半導体株の重しに－投資テーマは維持との声
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 世界的なAI企業の経営トップからAI開発の減速を求める声が相次ぎ、週明け14日の株式市場では半導体メーカーやサプライチェーン関連など、AI関連株の重しとなる可能性がある。ただ、市場関係者は堅調な投資需要を背景に、長期的な影響は限定的とみている。

米アンソロピックのダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（CEO）は12日、AIが人類に「深刻な」リスクを及ぼすとの懸念を示し、AI業界は新たなモデルの開発ペースを落とす必要があると訴えた。安全対策に十分な時間をかける考えを示した。

OpenAIのサム・アルトマンCEOや、xAIを率いるイーロン・マスク氏もアモデイ氏の訴えに賛同。アルトマン氏は安全性確保に集中するためOpenAIの年内上場を見送る方向だと、米経済誌フォーチュンのインタビューで明らかにした。

オールスプリング・グローバル・インベストメンツのポートフォリオマネジャー、ゲーリー・タン氏は「短期的な圧力にはなり得るが、長期的なAIトレードを頓挫させる可能性は低い」と話す。技術が急速に進化する中、他のAI開発者が「現在の序列を受け入れ、開発ペースを落とすことに同意するかは分からない」と指摘した。

背景には、AIを巡る開発競争がすでに世界的な規模に拡大していることがある。シンガポールのマルチファミリーオフィス、リード・キャピタルのジェラルド・ガン最高投資責任者（CIO）も、AI開発が巨大産業となりつつあるだけに、新規参入組、既存プレーヤーともに現在の開発ペースを維持することになりそうだと話す。

AIへの巨額投資に見合う利益を企業が上げられるのかとの懸念が、割高なAI関連株の重しとなっている。ナスダック100指数や米半導体株指数は6月に最高値を付けた後は下落し、S&P500種株価指数をアンダーパフォームしている。

T&Dアセットマネジメントの浪岡宏チーフ・ストラテジストは、AI関連企業トップの発言は短期的な逆風となる可能性があるものの、半導体などの需給逼迫は続いており、影響は限定的と分析。売り圧力を受けやすい銘柄群として、これまで上昇してきた電線株などを挙げた。

items.title: 中国主席、オープンソースAIなどで協力強化を提案－BRICS首脳会議
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国の習近平国家主席は、インドの首都ニューデリーで開かれた有力新興国グループ、BRICSの首脳会議で、学習・推論のソースコード（プログラムの設計図）などを公開するオープンソースAIや貿易・投資、デジタル産業、スマート製造、科学技術人材の各分野で協力を強化する五つのイニシアチブを提案した。国営の新華社通信が13日に伝えた。

習主席は演説で、大規模言語モデル（LLM）の開発・運用での協力推進に向け、中国主導で「BRICSオープンソースAIプラットフォーム」を構築する用意があると明らかにした。

さらにBRICS経済特区パートナーシップの創設を提案し、中国がBRICSサービス貿易フォーラムを来年主催すると述べた。

習氏はまた、開発途上国の代表権と発言力を高める国際金融アーキテクチャー（仕組み）改革を訴え、世界貿易機関（WTO）改革も正しい方向性を維持するよう強く求めた。円滑な産業サプライチェーンの安定維持、統合市場の育成、伝統産業のアップグレード、新興・未来産業の振興も提言した。
